cards.title: What is respect?
body: Respect is important in **daily life**. It can be shown in many ways.
We can respect **ourselves**, **other people**, **our country** and **the environment**.

cards.title: Kinds of respect
body: Tap the dots.

cards.title: Self-respect
body: Respect **begins** with respecting **yourself**. This is called **self-respect**.
To respect yourself, you should **know about yourself**.

cards.title: Why pen friends?

Her description has her **physical traits** and her **hobbies**.

steps.text: Daniel plays with his new ball. A **cat** walks on the fence. He shouts "Go away!"
He **throws the ball** at the cat. He misses. The ball flies over the fence.
**SMASH!** The neighbours' **flowerpot** is broken.
He puts the pieces in his pocket and **turns the broken side** to the wall. Nobody sees him.
His mother asks, "Where have you been?" He wants to hide it... but thinks: "No, I have to **tell the truth**."
He tells her **everything** and shows the pieces. He **feels good**, and he **learned from his mistake**.

body: **Socrates** lived long ago in **ancient Greece**. He was a respected **philosopher**, remembered for his **wisdom**.

Filter 2: **GOODNESS**. Is it about good qualities? It was **the opposite**.
Filter 3: **USEFULNESS**. Is it useful? The man said **no**.

cards.title: Filter before you talk
body: Before he listened to talk about his friend, Socrates asked **three questions**.

cards.title: Summary
body: Respect is the **foundation** of all positive relationships.
Showing respect = recognizing the worth of others and **treating them the way I want to be treated**.
With respect we avoid **degrading, insulting or injuring** others.
We have to be **truthful, good and useful** to our friends.

cards.title: Six qualities
body: Tap each quality.

steps.text: The English teacher gives a **dictation test**.
Ali cannot remember how to spell "**knowledge**".
His friend **Dawit** tells him to copy.
Ali **refuses**. He decided **not to cheat**.
He writes "knowledge" **without the letter K**. Some classmates laugh.
Ali is **not ashamed** to learn from his mistake. He is **happy** he did not cheat.

cards.title: Conscious of time
body: Good students know **time** is one of the most valuable things for success in school.
**Delaying** tasks like assignments and reading can stop you reaching your goals.

steps.text: Semir always **postpones** tasks.
His father explains the **value of time**. Semir promises to change.
Semir **wins first prize** in a singing competition. He must collect it **the same day**.
He goes **the next day**. The prize is a **concert ticket** for the day before: useless!
From then on Semir **learnt his lesson**.

cards.title: I love my teacher
body: In the poem, the teacher makes the student **want to learn**. She makes things **easier to understand**. She is **compassionate and smart**.

cards.title: Come to our class
body: Two poems describe two classes, **7A** and **7B**.
Class 7A is **noisy**, with **lazy** students. Its monitors do not do their job.
Class 7B is **friendly** and fun, but **Fafo** is always fighting.
The book asks: which class would **you** want to join, and why?

steps.text: Father sends **Birhane** to ask about chickens. He needs **three trips**: 50 for sale... 20 Naqfa each... they can sell tomorrow.
Father sends **Abrham**. In **one trip** he learns: 100 chickens, 18 Naqfa each if they buy 50, delivery tomorrow, and 19 Naqfa for more.

cards.title: Why Abrham got more responsibility
body: Abrham **thought ahead** and brought **all the information** and a **better price**.
Birhane now understood why his younger brother got more responsibility and rewards.

cards.title: Reading every day
body: To build a reading habit, read **every day**: morning, night, or lunch break.
You only need **20–30 minutes a day**. Read because it is **fun**, as a **hobby**.
A riddle poem called "The …" describes a building full of books: the **library**.

cards.title: Extra time

If you spend **extra time** studying, your grades go up and your knowledge increases.

cards.title: Everyone has a culture
body: Culture includes our **languages**, **music and dances**, **foods**, **manners**, **holidays and ceremonies**, and what we **wear** on special occasions.

cards.title: Everyone has a culture
body: Three things are true for every person.

cards.title: Culture is learned
body: We learn our **behaviours and beliefs** from the people we grow up with.
Students from another culture would answer the worksheet **differently**.

cards.title: Features of culture
body: Examples: **styles of dress** (Luweit, Sire Birki) and **foods** (Tikushm, porridge).
More: religious holidays, respect, folk tales, musical instruments, dancing, types of houses.
Also the **values of our revolution** (comradeship, heroism) and traditions of our struggle (candlelight, moment of silence).

cards.title: An iceberg
body: An iceberg is very huge. Only about **one-eighth** of it is **above the water**. The rest is below.

cards.title: Culture is like an iceberg
body: Tap the parts.

cards.title: Visible and invisible
body: **Visible**: things you can observe, like **styles of dress**.
**Invisible**: things you can only imagine, like **rules of polite behaviour**.
The visible part is only a **small part** of a much bigger whole.

lessons.title: Eritrea: a country of diverse cultures

cards.title: Nine ethnic groups
body: Eritrea has **nine ethnic groups**: Tigre, Tigrigna, Afar, Saho, Rashaida, Bedawet, Nara, Kunama and Bilen.
They are diverse, but they **share common cultural features**.

cards.title: Common cultural features
body: Things all nine ethnic groups share. Tap each one.

cards.title: Monochrome or polychrome?
body: "Monochrome" means **single colour**. Polychrome means many colours.

cards.title: Diversity is beautiful
body: A colour TV or a house with rooms of **different colours** shows how **variety** can make life richer.
Diversity is necessary for the **beauty and richness** of life.

cards.title: Dagu
body: Sometimes two Afar people meet while travelling in **opposite directions**.
They tell each other what they have **seen or heard** on the way.
This custom is called "**dagu**".

cards.title: Is it true for all Eritreans?
body: Some people from outside make comments like "Eritreans are very friendly and **hospitable**."
The book asks you to think: is each comment true for **all**, **some**, or **no** Eritreans?

cards.title: Rich oral traditions
body: All nine ethnic groups have rich **oral traditions**: songs, proverbs, riddles and sayings.

steps.text: **1868**: **Ras Alula Engida** from Tigrai invades Nara and Kunama villages in **Gashbarka**.
The lords' **livestock** are raided.
The local chief **Kaakaay** rises. All the people join.
**Aray Agabaa** marches with spears and swords.
They never kneel to the invader. The invading force is **demolished**.

cards.title: Riddles
body: A **riddle** is a question that needs thinking to find its answer.
The class can form two groups and challenge each other with riddles.

cards.title: Religion in Eritrea
body: **Islam** and **Christianity** are the most practised religions in Eritrea.
A few from the **Kunama** ethnic group worship the god/goddess **Ana**.

"It is **Easter**. I will go to my friend **Gebriela's** house for lunch. I will help her wash the dishes."

cards.title: Religious harmony
body: Helps: asking a friend about their **feast and fasting days**, joining a **peace march**, schools teaching **common values**.
Does not help: saying "My religion is older and **better** than yours."

cards.title: Unity in diversity
body: The nine groups have different religions, dress, hair styles, foods, dances and languages.
But they **share many common values**, passed from our forefathers and nurtured in the **struggle for independence**.

body: People start revolutions for various reasons. The **main reason** is to have your **rights respected**.
We cannot live without our family. We also cannot live without **a government of our own** and a **peaceful country**.

steps.text: **May 1957**, Asmara. Aboy Nafie is a grade 10 student. Families are very poor.
The principal announces: **Amharic** is the official language. Students must sing the **Ethiopian anthem** and raise the **Ethiopian flag**.
Students march in Asmara: "We don't want to learn in Amharic."
For **four days** more schools join. The protest **spreads** to other parts of Eritrea.

The enemy is weakened: thousands killed, thousands of weapons captured.

cards.title: Fighting alone
body: Eritrea's war was fought **without military aid** from any country.

**May 19, 1991**: Dekemhare is captured.
**May 24, 1991**: the fighters enter **Asmara**.
**May 26, 1991**: **Assab**, the final city, is liberated. Eritrea is free!
